vibe: Supply-chain compromises and cloud availability lead a busy security day, while new frontier models and open inference tooling keep the AI race moving at full speed.

cyber.title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA
cyber.summary: Multiple ransomware groups are exploiting a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass flaw to get around MFA. Treat exposed appliances as urgent: patch, hunt for compromise and rotate credentials.

cyber.title: OVHcloud CLI releases backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
cyber.summary: Five published OVHcloud CLI releases were replaced with secret-stealing malware. Anyone who installed affected GitHub binaries should assume cloud credentials and developer tokens may be compromised.

cyber.title: Critical FortiSIEM Flaw Gets Public Exploit PoC for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
cyber.summary: A public proof-of-concept is now available for an unauthenticated FortiSIEM remote-code-execution flaw. Internet-facing deployments need immediate patching and exposure review.

cyber.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
cyber.summary: Recently fixed Plex Media Server vulnerabilities are now being exploited to install malware. Update any reachable server and review it for suspicious activity.

cyber.title: ConnectWise customers hit by supply-chain attack linked to compromised API secret
cyber.summary: A compromised API secret enabled a supply-chain attack affecting ConnectWise cloud-backup customers. The vendor reset credentials while services remained disrupted; customers should rotate integrations and review access.

cyber.title: Russian APT28 Breaches NATO Naval Shipbuilder in NATO Country, Deploys New Reflective Loader
cyber.summary: APT28 breached a NATO-country naval shipbuilder and deployed a new reflective loader in a wider espionage campaign. Defence-adjacent organisations should review the reported tradecraft and hunt accordingly.

cyber.title: Hackers Use Autonomous AI Agents to Breach Company Websites, Target Over 1,200 Sites
cyber.summary: Attackers used an AI penetration-testing tool to automate reconnaissance and exploitation across more than 1,200 sites. The story is a concrete sign that agentic offensive tooling is moving from demos into campaigns.

cyber.title: EMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
cyber.summary: A reported intermediate certificate-authority compromise drew heavy security attention and coincided with Go blocking multiple CA keys. Certificate trust stores and emergency revocation paths are the operational issue to watch.

cyber.title: WordPress SEO plugin Rank Math compromised to backdoor websites
cyber.summary: The Rank Math WordPress plugin supply chain was compromised to backdoor sites. Operators should update, verify plugin integrity and inspect affected installations.

cyber.title: Nikkei discloses third data breach in a month, 1.8M records exposed
cyber.summary: Nikkei disclosed a third breach in a month, this time involving 1.8 million records. The repeat incidents make containment and identity protection more important than the headline count alone.

cyber.title: Possible new Cellebrite iPhone Radio Zero-Day
cyber.summary: Researchers are examining signs of a possible iPhone radio-layer zero-day associated with Cellebrite tooling. Details remain limited, so this is one to monitor rather than act on blindly.

cyber.title: Grocery giant Ahold Delhaize confirms cyberattack forced US and European systems offline
cyber.summary: Ahold Delhaize confirmed a cyberattack disrupted systems across US and European operations, another reminder that retail incidents quickly become availability and supply-chain events.

ai.title: Gemini 4 Argon is now available for everyone
ai.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Argon broadly available. Early benchmarks put it near the frontier for reasoning and long-context work, though coding results appear more mixed and should be tested against real workloads.

ai.title: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol is dramatically better at migrating legacy code
ai.summary: OpenAI is positioning GPT-6.1 Sol for low-resource languages and legacy-code migration, including COBOL-heavy estates. The practical test is whether generated migrations survive enterprise validation and integration constraints.

ai.title: DeepSeek Open-Sources DeepInfer, the Inference Framework Behind DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
ai.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the high-performance serving framework behind V4.1 Flash. It is immediately relevant to teams optimising throughput and cost for self-hosted inference.

ai.title: Google Open-Sources TorchTPU, a Native PyTorch Backend for Cloud TPUs
ai.summary: TorchTPU gives PyTorch a native backend for Google TPUs, lowering the friction of moving familiar training and inference code onto Google Cloud accelerators.

ai.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
ai.summary: US civilian agencies were ordered to remove DeepSeek products, turning model provenance and data-handling concerns into a concrete government procurement restriction.

ai.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
ai.summary: Hidden instructions in WhatsApp help content reportedly steered AI systems away from recommending privacy regulators. It is a sharp example of web content being shaped for machine readers rather than humans.

ai.title: Voxtral 3
ai.summary: Mistral introduced Voxtral 3, renewing competition in speech and audio models. Worth a look for teams evaluating transcription, voice interfaces or local deployment options.

ai.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
ai.summary: ChatGPT added per-chat locking, a useful privacy control for shared devices even though it is not a substitute for account security or organisational data policy.

ai.title: Inception Releases Mercury 3 Diffusion LLM at 1,068 Tokens per Second
ai.summary: Mercury 3 claims extremely high token throughput using a diffusion-language-model architecture. The speed is eye-catching; quality, serving cost and workload fit need independent testing.

ai.title: An AI Agent Joined a Listserv of Top Internet Researchers. The Reply-All Chaos Is Still Unfolding
ai.summary: An AI agent entered a research mailing list and triggered a reply-all mess, neatly illustrating why autonomous agents need identity, permission and participation boundaries.

it.title: Google Cloud says a 'power event' caused today's outage
it.summary: A power event in Google Cloud’s London region disrupted multiple services and spilled into banking availability. The useful cloud-engineering lesson is to re-check regional dependencies and failover assumptions.

it.title: OpenBSD 8.0
it.summary: OpenBSD 8.0 landed with the project’s usual security-first platform updates. It is worth reviewing for network appliances, hardened hosts and upstream changes that may flow into other BSD ecosystems.

it.title: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust
it.summary: Cloudflare published Tsrs, a TypeScript port to Rust. It is another serious attempt to improve performance and maintainability in JavaScript tooling while retaining ecosystem compatibility.

it.title: Swamped curl maintainers take low-level flaws public to survive vulnerability 'avalanche'
it.summary: curl maintainers are changing vulnerability handling under a flood of low-severity reports. The episode highlights the triage burden that automated security submissions can impose on core open-source projects.

it.title: Microsoft admits that Always On VPN problems were not fixed in the October Security Update
it.summary: Microsoft says October’s security update did not fully resolve Always On VPN failures. Windows infrastructure teams should validate the workaround and avoid assuming the issue is closed.

it.title: RAM prices are crazy high, but do not settle for an 8GB laptop
it.summary: Memory prices remain elevated, but 8GB is increasingly inadequate for development and local AI work. The buying advice is simple: protect useful lifespan before chasing the lowest sticker price.

videos.title: Did Google just dethrone OpenAI and Anthropic?
videos.verdict: WATCH — a fast, sceptical hands-on comparison rather than a benchmark recital.
videos.summary: Fireship tests Gemini 4 Argon against GPT-6 and Claude across coding, 3D and media tasks. Argon leads some reasoning and long-context benchmarks and is aggressively priced, but its web-development coding result and generated-video quality are less convincing.

videos.title: The Problem with Jev: Can You Trust AI Decisions?
videos.verdict: WATCH — especially if you design automated security or operations workflows.
videos.summary: IBM’s Jeff Crume argues that confidence is not evidence: decision models should be treated as untrusted components. His practical prescription is input validation, independent signals, audit logs, drift detection and human escalation for high-risk actions.

videos.title: Hippocratic AI powers safe, conversational voice agents for healthcare with Google Cloud
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful architecture numbers, but it is a customer case study.
videos.summary: Hippocratic AI describes healthcare voice agents running on GKE with sub-500ms first-token time and roughly 1.5-second turn latency. The strongest detail is its large-scale Gemini-driven evaluation pipeline; the safety claims are vendor-supplied.

videos.title: How do I upgrade my ElastiCache for Redis or Valkey engine version?
videos.verdict: SKIM — practical only when planning an upgrade.
videos.summary: AWS walks through backing up and upgrading ElastiCache, including Redis-to-Valkey moves and rollback. Schedule for low write traffic, back up first and expect only brief write interruption on modern engine versions.
